## Purpose

The `Ac`-prefixed types are the acceptance-criterion domain of the review family: `AcItem` (one criterion parsed out of the spec markdown), `AcResult` (one execution outcome), `AcProof` (one criterion's record in the proof ledger) and `AcProofLedger` (the on-disk `ac-proof.json`). They exist so the crate has exactly ONE parser and ONE executor behind every consumer — QA, the negative test, the ANALYZE linter and the amendment door all read the same criterion through the same seam. Each new fact about a criterion becomes a COLUMN in `AcProof`, never an overwrite of an earlier one: `proof`, `control`, `confirmation` and `removal` record four different passes and are kept apart on purpose. The types carry their own justification in doc comments, because the distinctions (NEVER TAKEN vs TAKEN-AND-GREEN) are the whole reason the enums have more than two variants.

## Convention

One `.rs` module per `run` subcommand under `apps/rt/src/commands/review/` (`ac_negative_check.rs`, `analyze_validation.rs`, `qa_run/`), snake_case file names matching the published kebab-case command. Roughly a dozen `Ac*` declarations live here today. Visibility is `pub(crate)` by default — `pub` only when an integration test or another crate face needs it. Serde types carry `#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]`, every column added after the first release carries `#[serde(default)]`, and a column's "nobody asked" state is the enum's `#[default]` variant so an older ledger parses into the truth about itself.

## How to apply

A new criterion-level fact goes into `AcProof` as a new `#[serde(default)]` field plus its own `Copy` enum whose default variant means NOT TAKEN; add a `classify_<pass>` pure total function beside the existing classify family and a `const REASON_*: &str` naming the ONE action that clears each non-clearing value. Never add a second parser or a second command executor — call `qa_run::parse_ac_items` / `qa_run::execute_ac`; never re-derive the project root from `current_dir()`, take it as a `root: &Path` parameter (this tool runs from worktrees). Keep the ledger byte-stable: entries sorted by id, no timestamps, repo-relative forward-slash paths. Reading `ac-proof.json` goes through the single loader and lookup rule in `ac_negative_check`. If the work adds a `run` subcommand, do all four registrations from the crate Guards.

## Examples

- Ref: `apps/rt/src/commands/review/ac_negative_check.rs` — `AcProof`/`AcProofLedger`, the four pass columns, classify plus `REASON_*` pairs.
- Ref: `apps/rt/src/commands/review/qa_run/mod.rs` — `AcItem`, `AcResult` (private fields plus read-only accessors so an execution cannot be forged), `execute_ac`.
- Ref: `apps/rt/src/commands/review/analyze_validation.rs` — a consumer reading the ledger through the producer's door instead of restating its rules.
